title: Freeze API and extension boundaries
goal: Choose the final supported consumer/implementer surface and typed seams that let modules supply behavior without importing core internals.
context: Architecture phase B. Approximate size: L. This is the single planned pre-1.0 contract transition, including mixed namespaces, entry point, scope semantics, typing and publication. Detailed PHP signatures, tasks and exact check commands are authored in a separate phase-design session from the fixed semantics.

consumes: The qualified persistence and safety contract from the preceding phase
produces: Typed core scope/query, change-pipe and participant semantics
boundaries: Core owns mandatory decision and write stages
Modules exchange only core contracts/values, with no sibling bridges or plugin-ID dependencies
No public coordinator/session/mutation leakage and no dynamic macro API

include: Contracts, Context, Tenancy and mixed Scopes signatures
Plugin compilation, immutable options and capability compatibility
State token serialization, finite enums and API manifest coverage
exclude: One interface or Composer package per internal service
Repeated naming redesign after the candidate boundary

pitfalls: Consumer compatibility differs from implementer/subclass compatibility
Readonly runtime inputs may still borrow mutable host models
A module-table capability returning a raw connection defeats its boundary
A facade without declared methods evades the present manifest

validation.procedure: Classify every supported type/member/override point and verify signature closure; compile valid built-in and independent consumer contributions through the same slots; reject duplicates, invalid types, unsupported capabilities, unchecked context writes and invariant-bypassing continuation/results.
validation.expect: Every supported symbol has one stable owner; external extensions need no internal/core-to-module dependency and cannot bypass final validation through supported slots.

deliverables: Typed extension semantics and compatibility rules
Member-aware manifest generator and frozen candidate surface
Single upgrade map and non-PHP contract inventory

sections.title: Exit criterion
sections.text: All supported signatures and extension semantics have a stable owner; scope behavior, audit persistence and tools can be moved without inventing another public mechanism during implementation.
